verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents a REST API with a dedicated `GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results` endpoint for pulling analysis programmatically. Its official MCP server lets AI tools make authenticated REST calls, so an agent can retrieve results and use Chance to Win to reason about winners. However, reading experiment configuration programmatically is only implied by the generic 'full REST API' claim rather than a documented endpoint, and nothing shows support for ship/rollback recommendations. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented experiment-configuration read endpoint, documented agent workflows for summarizing results and recommending ship/rollback, a published OpenAPI spec (the probe returned 404), and independent hands-on corroboration of agent results retrieval.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can read experiment configurations and results programmatically to summarize outcomes and recommend ship/rollback decisions

citations.quote: Get results for an experiment (`GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results`) to pull the latest analysis into your own reporting.
GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.
The official GrowthBook MCP server is a thin bridge: it loads GrowthBook Agent Skills (workflows and guardrails) and makes authenticated calls to the GrowthBook REST API.
Connect AI tools like Cursor, VS Code, and Claude to GrowthBook using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Chance to Win tells you the probability that the variation is better. Anything above 95% ... is highlighted green indicating a very clear winner.
